title: eludite.terminal.wait input
description: Wait until a terminal shows something, up to `timeout_ms` (default 10000, at most 60000): its next prompt (`prompt: true`, the default when neither `pattern` nor `exit` is given: the command you sent finished; with shell integration the answer has its exit code), output matching `pattern` (a regular expression, Rust syntax, searched in what was printed after `mark`), or the shell's end (`exit: true`). Answers which happened (`matched`), the text printed after `mark` (the command's output, without the prompt when the shell's integration marks them) and the `mark` to pass next time. Use it after eludite.terminal.send instead of sleeping. Not satisfied in time answers `matched: "timeout"`, not a failure. When the person types into the terminal while you wait, the wait ends at once with `interrupted_by: "user"`, and your next eludite.terminal.send is refused until you call eludite.terminal.read. Always allowed for agents (class read).

terminal.description: The terminal: its id from eludite.terminal.open or eludite.terminal.list (`term1`, `term2`, ...). Default: the active terminal of the Terminal window (the one last opened or selected).

mark.description: Wait for what comes after this mark. Default: your last eludite.terminal.send's mark, else the output's current end.

prompt.description: Wait for the next prompt after `mark`.

pattern.description: Wait for output after `mark` matching this regular expression (Rust regex syntax; `(?i)` for case-insensitive).

exit.description: Wait for the shell to end.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait, in milliseconds (default 10000).
